attention: The review repeatedly describes discovering the festival through verbs such as walk, follow your nose, sniff out, uncover and figure out.
ordered_material: You can’t walk into a gallery without learning about some subcultural genius or longlost creative you’ve never heard of.
You’ve just got to follow your nose and hope you sniff out something you like.
There are curated displays, satellite exhibitions, performances, off-site projects, and it’s impossible to figure out how any of it fits together.
Like a lot of people in EAF, she never showed her work publicly in her lifetime, and was only discovered after her death in 2013.
died having never shown any of the thousands of paintings and drawings he amassed over his lifetime
stayed unpublished and unseen in his lifetime
If contemporary artists and institutions want to tell hidden stories, I think they have a duty – to viewers and to their subjects – to tell them clearly.
I love it, but I’m not sure how the art downstairs fails to work so well.
open_question: What happens to the festival's language of wandering and stumbling when it is placed beside artists whose work went unseen until after their deaths?
